facts.text: The opera premiered in Rome on 20 February 1816 under a different title: Almaviva, o sia L’inutile precauzione.
facts.evidence: under the title Almaviva, o sia L'inutile precauzione) took place on 20 February 1816 at the Teatro Argentina, Rome

facts.text: The premiere was a disaster: the audience hissed and jeered throughout, and several on-stage accidents occurred.
facts.evidence: was a disaster: the audience hissed and jeered throughout, and several on-stage accidents occurred

facts.text: Many in the first-night crowd were fans of Giovanni Paisiello, whose own Barber of Seville was popular. The second performance, however, was a success.
evidence: many of the audience were supporters of one of Rossini's rivals, the veteran Giovanni Paisiello
The second performance, however, was successful.

facts.text: Rossini composed the score in just under three weeks.
facts.evidence: the music for Il barbiere di Siviglia was composed in just under three weeks

facts.text: The famous overture was recycled from two earlier Rossini operas, so it contains none of the Barber’s own tunes.
facts.evidence: the famous overture was actually recycled from two earlier Rossini operas, Aureliano in Palmira and Elizabeth, Queen of England and thus contains none of the thematic material

facts.text: Mozart’s Marriage of Figaro, composed 30 years earlier, is based on the sequel play in Beaumarchais’s Figaro trilogy.
facts.evidence: Mozart's opera The Marriage of Figaro, composed 30 years earlier in 1786, is based on the second part of the Beaumarchais trilogy

facts.text: In 1825 the Barber became the first opera ever performed in Italian in New York. The 17-year-old future Maria Malibran was in the cast.
evidence: became the first opera ever to be performed in Italian in New York
including the 17-year-old Maria-Felicia, later known as Maria Malibran

facts.text: Rosina was written for a contralto. Critic Richard Osborne calls turning her into a soprano the most serious distortion of Rossini’s intentions.
facts.attribution: Richard Osborne, New Grove Dictionary of Opera (via Wikipedia)
evidence: The role of Rosina was originally written for a contralto
The most serious distortion has been the upward transposition of the role of Rosina

facts.text: After Adelina Patti sang a very florid “Una voce poco fa”, Rossini reportedly asked: “Very nice, my dear, and who wrote the piece you have just performed?”
facts.evidence: Very nice, my dear, and who wrote the piece you have just performed?

facts.text: The Act II singing lesson often became “a show-stopping cabaret”: Nellie Melba accompanied herself on the piano, and Pauline Viardot inserted Alyabyev’s “Nightingale”.
evidence: The singing lesson in act 2 has often been turned into "a show-stopping cabaret"
Nellie Melba followed suit, accompanying herself on the piano in the final song
Pauline Viardot began the practice of inserting Alexander Alyabyev's "Nightingale"

facts.text: The Barber is considered one of the greatest masterpieces of comedy in music, “the opera buffa of all ‘opere buffe’”.
facts.evidence: considered to be one of the greatest masterpieces of comedy within music, and has been described as the opera buffa of all "opere buffe"

facts.text: Beaumarchais’s original play had a similar story: poorly received at first, then a favorite within a week.
facts.evidence: poorly received at first, only to become a favorite within a week
